site.name: Ajax Mine
overview: The Ajax Mine was a coal mine southwest of early Louisville. City historical research identifies Mahlon V. “Ajax” Johnson as its operator and shows that the mine influenced nearby town development during Louisville's coal-mining era.

In 1889 Johnson proposed a new community called Ajaxville near the mine. He later changed course, and in 1890 platted Johnson's First Addition for miners, tying the Ajax operation directly to Louisville's residential growth.

timeline.text: Contemporary newspaper accounts summarized by the Louisville Historical Museum describe Mahlon “Ajax” Johnson's proposal for an 'Ajaxville' development near the Ajax Mine he controlled.
Johnson platted Johnson's First Addition for miners. Louisville's historic residential context identifies him as the operator of the Ajax Mine southwest of the original town.

moreHistory: The Ajax Mine is part of the Louisville-area coal landscape that shaped settlement, employment and neighborhood development in eastern Boulder County.
Louisville's historic context places the mine southwest of the original town in what is now green space between East and West Lois Drive.
A mapped historic mine locality near 39.977763, -105.136652 provides a defensible identification point. Remnant does not represent it as a field-surveyed surviving shaft or opening.
